items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: who was a student of Julius Baker’s and she once said, “You never make a mistake, how is that?”

ctx.x: One thing I’ve discovered is when I’m stuck if I go and listen to music that is the total opposite of what I’m working on that sometimes the answer will be — it’ll seem like so obvious to me that I didn’t think of it, and it’s prompted by hearing something that has nothing to do with what I’m working on you know. But you’re right, problem solving. Because sometimes if you just think there should be a dissonant ensemble right here based on this melodic pattern. Well to work that out the idea that comes to you and…

something right away. You know basically most of what I practice is stuff that I want to integrate into my playing. Well the process of getting something under your fingers is a long process. And then to have it emerge naturally into your vocabulary as an improviser, you know, a lot of times by the time you get something under your fingers you’re bored with it. You practice it so much. But then it starts to come out in your playing, or fragments of it. I don’t want to be a guy who learns a lick and then you get…

It is. Have you ever had an instance where you were leading a big band and they were playing your music and a soloist sounded like they were practicing what they were working on during their solo, and it seemed to be a disconnect to the piece itself?
